title: Pathfinding Future PIM Architectures by Demystifying a Commercial PIM Technology
problem: Processing-in-memory has failed to achieve real-world adoption despite decades of research due to high design overheads and lack of killer applications. Understanding the architectural design space and limitations of commercial PIM systems is needed to guide next-generation PIM architecture development.
motivation: Commercial PIM technologies are now entering the market to address memory-intensive workloads, making empirical analysis of their design tradeoffs critical for future architecture improvements.
method: The researchers create uPIMulator, a simulation tool that takes code for the commercial UPMEM-PIM processor and converts it to the low-level machine instructions the hardware runs, then simulates execution one clock cycle at a time. Using this tool, they measure how UPMEM performs on different workloads and identify its architectural limitations.
key_novelty: uPIMulator is a cycle-by-cycle simulator of the commercial UPMEM-PIM processor that reveals architectural limitations to guide future PIM system design.
contributions: Development of uPIMulator - a flexible simulation framework for compiling and cycle-level simulation of UPMEM-PIM code
Detailed characterization study demystifying UPMEM-PIM architecture design and implementation
Identification of key architectural limitations in current UPMEM-PIM systems through empirical case studies
Architectural recommendations for future PIM systems based on characterization findings
